A single flat-sided hexagonal diorama tile, 32 m across, lush meadow grass cap and the hexagon side walls show a thin grass lip over dark root-filled topsoil that darkens softly downward into a near-black foot, one continuous dark earth. Near the middle of the tile stands one small timber-framed English village cottage: dark oak half-timbering over cream lime-plaster panels, a steep brown clay-tile roof with gables, tall red-brick chimneys with clay pots, and small-paned timber casement windows, with a gravel path to its front door, a small cottage garden and a low hedge. A few steps from the front door, beside the gravel path on a small round apron of flagstones, stands one roofed village well: a round waist-high well wall of rough weathered grey and buff fieldstones laid in pale lime mortar, noticeably wider than it is tall, topped with a flat ring of smooth pale grey dressed capstones, two stout dark oak posts rising from opposite sides of the wall to carry a small steep gabled roof of brown clay tiles with plain dark oak bargeboards, and between the posts under the roof a turned timber windlass axle with a small iron crank handle at one end, a coil of thick hemp rope wound on the axle and hanging down to a wooden bucket of timber staves bound with dark iron hoops, the bucket resting on the capstones beside the round opening. The well is about 1.5 m across, small beside the cottage, its roof ridge well below the cottage eaves.
